# Incident Report — MTA 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** (confirmed via ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.11.26.183` ↔ `arp.src.hw_mac`) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (NBNS name records `<00>`/`<20>` from 10.11.26.183) |
| Windows domain | nemotoads.health (NetBIOS: NEMOTODES), DC = NEMOTODES-DC / 10.11.26.3 |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** (Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic between 10.11.26.183 and the DC 10.11.26.3) |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** — attribution is **signature-confirmed**.

- IDS alerts fired directly on the traffic: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`, all sourced/destined 10.11.26.183 ↔ 194.180.191.64 at 04:50:45 UTC onward.
- Confirmed by following the TCP stream (stream 77, port 443, plaintext HTTP not TLS): requests carry `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, responses carry `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)`, and the protocol exchange uses NetSupport's native `CMD=POLL` / `CMD=ENCD` fields with base64/binary `DATA=` payloads — this is the tool's real client/server handshake, not a guess from naming.
- Delivery chain observed in DNS/TLS SNI immediately preceding infection: `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5) → `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139) and `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207), all resolved within the same ~5-second window at 04:50:11–04:50:16 UTC — consistent with a cracked-software lure page chained through a subscribe/notification-consent redirector. `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup / TLS SNI (modandcrackedapk .com)` alerts corroborate this is a known malicious "crack" distribution domain. A second `modandcrackedapk.com` TLS session at 04:50:40 UTC precedes the first C2 checkin by 5 seconds — this is almost certainly the payload download, but the download itself is TLS-encrypted in the capture, so the delivered file cannot be exported or hashed from this evidence.
- C2 beaconing (`POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm`) runs on a steady ~60-second interval from 04:50:45 UTC through the end of the capture (~04:43 the following hour), which is the classic NetSupport RAT keep-alive/poll cadence.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| c2_endpoint | **194.180.191.64:443** | Plaintext HTTP C2 (`fakeurl.htm`, `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD`), tcp.stream 77 and repeated streams every ~60s; matches `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` / `Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin` alerts |
| url | **http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm** | Exact request line in every C2 POST, `tshark -Y "http.request"` |
| domain | **modandcrackedapk.com** (→ 193.42.38.139) | DNS query + TLS SNI at 04:50:14–04:50:40 UTC; flagged by `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup / TLS SNI` |
| domain | **classicgrand.com** (→ 213.246.109.5) | DNS query 04:50:11 UTC, resolved immediately before the modandcrackedapk.com/confirmsubscription.com lookups — part of the redirect/lure chain |
| domain | **confirmsubscription.com** (→ 52.8.34.0, 13.56.30.207) | DNS query 04:50:14–15 UTC, same redirect window as the above |
| url | **http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp** | Plain HTTP GET at 04:50:45 UTC, immediately before first C2 checkin — the RAT's own geolocation self-check; flagged by `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request` |

No transferred executable/file could be exported or hashed: the payload delivery from `modandcrackedapk.com` occurred entirely over TLS, and `--export-objects http` over the full capture yielded only benign OS/browser artifacts (`connecttest.txt`, `ProcessMAU.txt`, CRL/CT files, and the C2's own `fakeurl.htm` POST/response bodies) — no downloaded binary is present in cleartext.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)

- `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `dns.msftncsi.com` — Windows connectivity checks
- `login.live.com`, `*.office.com`, `*.microsoft.com`, `edge.microsoft.com`, `checkappexec.microsoft.com` — normal Windows/Office/Edge telemetry
- `acroipm2.adobe.com`, `armmf.adobe.com` — Adobe update checks
- `code.jquery.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `www.gstatic.com`, `maps.googleapis.com`, `css/js.createsend1.com` — page resource loads consistent with the lure site's front end
- `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `r10.o.lencr.org` — Windows trusted-root/CRL updates
- SMB/EFSR/NTLMSSP alerts (`GPL NETBIOS SMB ...`, `ETPRO POLICY [MS-EFSR] ...`) between 10.11.26.183 and the domain controller 10.11.26.3 at 04:50:10 UTC — these are the workstation's normal (if legacy SMBv1) domain-join/Netlogon-style traffic to its own DC, not observed lateral movement; flagged only because the signatures alert on SMBv1 usage generically. Treated as context, not a confirmed indicator.

## Incident Summary

The domain-joined workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as user **oboomwald** on the nemotoads.health domain, was infected with **NetSupport RAT** after browsing through a redirect chain (`classicgrand.com` → `modandcrackedapk.com` fake cracked-software site, with `confirmsubscription.com` in the same chain) around 04:50 UTC on 2024-11-26. The malware performed a self geolocation check against `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` and then established persistent C2 over plaintext HTTP disguised on port 443 to **194.180.191.64**, POSTing to `/fakeurl.htm` with a NetSupport Manager/Gateway `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` protocol on a ~60-second beacon interval for the remainder of the capture.
